decisions.statement: A limit on processor time slows the thing limited rather than ending it.
A ceiling is stated as processor time over a period, and both are part of it.
A thing at its ceiling waits for the next period rather than being refused.
A ceiling holds even where every other processor is idle.
A share decides who goes first only while more than one thing wants a processor.
A share left unspent by one thing is taken by another rather than kept.
Every agent, service and container on the workstation runs under a stated share.
The desktop outranks the apps, and the apps outrank everything akasha runs.
A run past its processor ceiling runs to its end rather than being stopped there.
What a run past its ceiling judged does not land.
A run stopped partway leaves the agent nothing to mend that run by.
Every processor limit is the value of a page property.
Refusing what a run answered is how a processor ceiling is enforced.
A processor ceiling drives down what a run spends rather than keeping the host safe from that run.

definition: the most processor time one thing may take, and what happens when it wants more
